title: Relative module flatness at a space point is independent of the etale chart
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $T$ be an $S$-scheme. Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $f:X\to T$ and let $M$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module on the small etale site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. For any representable etale scheme chart $e:U\to X$, let $M_U$ be the quasi-coherent Zariski module corresponding to $e^*M$ under [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], using tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. For a point $x\in|X|$ [def-a1-space-point-topology], the following are equivalent: (a) for some such chart and some $u\in U$ over $x$, $(M_U)_u$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{T,f(x)}$; (b) for every such chart and every $u\in U$ over $x$, $(M_U)_u$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{T,f(x)}$. Stalks mean ordinary Zariski stalks [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk]; relative flatness and module flatness use [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over, def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Equivalently, for any geometric representative $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ of $x$, with $\Omega$ algebraically closed and $\bar t=f\bar x$, the geometric stalk $M_{\bar x}$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{T,\bar t}$. These geometric stalks are the colimits over pointed etale scheme neighbourhoods. No finiteness, separation or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 05VU (lemma-flat-at-point), equivalence (1) and (2), and its proof, which starts with an arbitrary chart diagram; target chart specialized to the identity of the scheme T.

proof.text: Fix a geometric representative $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ of $x$, and any chart $e:U\to X$ and point $u\in U$ over $x$. By [lem-sfb-etale-geometric-point-specified-lift], there is a lift $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ centered at this specified $u$, without enlarging $\Omega$. Put $t=f(x)$, $R=\mathcal O_{T,t}$, $B=\mathcal O_{U,u}$ and $N=(M_U)_u$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-strict-local-flatness] to $e$ and to the identity chart of $T$: the natural germ maps identify $\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}=B^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and $\mathcal O_{T,\bar t}=R^{\mathrm{sh}}$, with the residue embeddings furnished by the geometric points. By [lem-sfb-space-quasicoherent-geometric-stalk-tensor], $N\otimes_B B^{\mathrm{sh}}\simeq M_{\bar x}$. This isomorphism respects the $R$-action through $fe$: a local function germ on $T$ acts on either side by its pullback germ on a common pointed neighbourhood. Hence the $R$-action is the restriction of the given $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$-action.

source.place: Tag 05VU (lemma-flat-at-point), proof with target chart the identity of T.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-strict-henselization-faithfully-flat], $B\to B^{\mathrm{sh}}$ is faithfully flat. Apply [lem-trf-flatness-faithfully-flat-extension] to $R\to B\to B^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and the $B$-module $N$. It gives $N$ flat over $R$ if and only if $B^{\mathrm{sh}}\otimes_B N$ is flat over $R$. The tensor symmetry $b\otimes n\mapsto n\otimes b$, whose inverse has the same formula, and step 1 identify this last module with $M_{\bar x}$ as an $R$-module. Finally [lem-sfb-strict-henselization-module-flatness], applied to the $R^{\mathrm{sh}}$-module $M_{\bar x}$, makes this equivalent to flatness over $R^{\mathrm{sh}}=\mathcal O_{T,\bar t}$. Thus the ordinary stalk criterion at every specified chart point is equivalent to the geometric criterion for every specified geometric representative. No flatness of $R\to B$ has been assumed.

proof.text: There is at least one chart point over $x$: take a surjective etale scheme atlas as in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Base change it by a field-valued representative of $x$, which exists by [def-a1-space-point-topology]. The resulting scheme is nonempty by the scheme-test definition of surjectivity; any of its points maps to a point $u$ of the atlas over $x$. By [def-weil-algebraic-closure] choose an algebraic closure of $\kappa(u)$; its residue-field embedding defines a geometric point of the atlas centered at $u$ by [def-weil-geometric-point]. Composing with the atlas gives a geometric representative of $x$. These choices require no finiteness or separation assumption.

source.place: Tag 05VU (lemma-flat-at-point), proof with target chart the identity of T.

proof.text: Assume (a), and choose its chart point. For any geometric representative of $x$, step 2 at that point gives the geometric flatness condition. Conversely, assume the geometric condition for one geometric representative of $x$. For every chart and every point over $x$, step 2 gives the ordinary flatness condition, hence (b). Condition (b) implies (a) by the chart-point existence in step 3. This proves the equivalence of (a), (b), and the geometric condition for any representative, including equivalence of the existential and universal readings of the latter. If $X$ is empty there is no $x$ to check; a non-surjective chart missing $x$ contributes no points to (b), while the atlas still supplies a witness for (a).

lean.statement: theorem module_flat_point_chart_independence {S : Scheme.{u}} {X : AlgebraicSpace S} {T : Over S} (f : X ⟶ schemeSpace T) (M : X.Modules) (hM : M.IsQuasicoherent) (x : Point X.obj.obj) : ((∃ (U : X.EtaleSite) (u : X.etaleForget.obj U), schemePointMap U.obj.hom u = x ∧ ModuleIsFlatAtChartPoint f M U u) ↔ ∀ (U : X.EtaleSite) (u : X.etaleForget.obj U), schemePointMap U.obj.hom u = x → ModuleIsFlatAtChartPoint f M U u) ∧ (∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (s : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ S) (xbar : yoneda.obj (Over.mk s) ⟶ X.obj.obj), Quot.mk _ (PointRepresentative.mk Ω s (yonedaEquiv xbar)) = x → ((∃ (U : X.EtaleSite) (u : X.etaleForget.obj U), schemePointMap U.obj.hom u = x ∧ ModuleIsFlatAtChartPoint f M U u) ↔ Module.Flat (SingleComplex.stalkRing s (xbar ≫ f.hom.hom)) ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (SingleComplex.stalkMap f s xbar)).obj ((SingleComplex.stalkModel s xbar).modules.obj M))))
